subject: Data Science & Machine Learning
error_analysis:
v3 held-out test run, 33 questions (28 answerable, 5 not in the books), 2026-10-18. Settings as v2.1 (chosen on the validation split): Toodles Ultra (qwen2.5:1.5b, Q4_K_M, Ollama 0.40.5, fully on the GeForce MX450 GPU). Books 014 and 015 were replaced the same day by freely licensed books (Machine Learning: A First Course for Engineers and Scientists; Patterns, Predictions, and Actions) because permission for the two commercial titles could not be confirmed. The index was rebuilt (22,216 passages) and six questions tied to the old books were updated beforehand (test: Q019 and Q032 rewritten; validation: Q018, Q049, Q050, Q051), so 31 of the 33 test questions are unchanged from v2.1. Full write-up: docs/evaluation_report.md.

1. Retrieval: hit rate 60.7% (v2.1: 53.6%), +/-1 page 67.9%, recall@5 55.4%; target 80%. Q025 now retrieves its page and the rewritten Q019 finds both of its pages. Validation fell from 80% to 75% (Q047 lost its page to passages from the new books). Kinds of miss: front matter (title, contents, notation and preface pages) retrieved for questions that name a book (Q031, Q032, Q038, Q041); cross-book and citation-check questions miss at least one expected page (Q030, Q031, Q032, Q034, Q041, Q042; 0 of 6 hits); relevant pages elsewhere that expected_evidence does not list (Q005, Q012, Q015, Q021); explanations crossing a page break (Q024, Q030 are hits within +/-1 page).

2. Abstention: 3 of 5 no-answer questions refused. Q035 (AWS SageMaker) was answered from D2L's appendix on renting AWS machines; Q038 (Python 3.13) got an unrelated quote from the fallback. 3 of 28 answerable questions were wrongly refused (10.7%; v2.1 7.1%): Q025 and Q029 (calculations) and Q041 (evidence page not retrieved).

3. Citations and answers: 100% of citations resolve to stored passages; 52.0% of cited pages are expected evidence pages. Automatic scores: F1 0.309, similarity 0.813 (quote-only baseline 0.209 / 0.765). Reading the answers: Q031 calls The Elements of Statistical Learning 'ISLR'; Q042 is a quote fallback with a formula from another book; on validation Q051 gives an accuracy of 85% instead of 90%, which the word-overlap check cannot catch.

4. Speed: mean 8.4 s, p95 12.1 s per answer on the GPU (v2.1: 6.5 / 9.9 s); evaluation process peak RAM 0.8 GB plus about 1.4 GB for Ollama; index 61.2 MB.

5. Answer correctness and groundedness: human review pending (evaluation/human_reviews.json is empty).

Not changed after seeing these test results. Candidate fixes to check on the validation split first: leave title, contents and preface pages out of the index; one retrieval per book named in cross-book questions; require several question keywords in a fallback quote; number-aware grounding for computed values; embed passages with max_seq_length 512 or shorter chunks (50% of passages exceed 256 tokens); and complete expected_evidence lists for topics covered in several books.
limitations: Retrieval is below the 80% target (test 60.7%, validation 75%), and exact-page evidence matching undercounts valid pages in other chapters and books. Half of the passages exceed the 256-token embedding limit, so their endings count only for keyword search. Title, contents and preface pages are indexed. The lexical grounding check compares words, not meaning: it can pass an on-topic but misleading answer (Q035) or a wrong number (Q051), and the quote fallback can quote loosely related text (Q038, Q042). The 1.5B model rarely carries out calculations correctly. Answers on the GPU can vary slightly between runs. The automatic answer scores are not a substitute for the pending human review of correctness and groundedness. Evaluation questions and reference answers are drafts that still need subject-expert review; validation and test share 8 evidence pages (no near-duplicate questions). Permission is documented for all 15 books, but the coordinator has not yet approved the books or models. Passages never cross page boundaries; equations and tables lose their layout.
